title: Chapter 1: What Is Photosynthesis?
paragraphs: Plants don't eat food the way we do. Instead, they make their own food using sunlight, water, and a gas from the air called carbon dioxide. This process is called photosynthesis.
The word comes from two parts: 'photo' means light, and 'synthesis' means putting things together. So photosynthesis literally means 'putting together with light.'
Almost every living thing on Earth depends on photosynthesis, even animals and humans — because it's how plants make the oxygen we breathe and the food that feeds the entire food chain.

title: Chapter 2: The Ingredients a Plant Needs
paragraphs: A plant needs three things to make food: sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide. Water travels up from the roots through the stem, while carbon dioxide enters through tiny pores in the leaves called stomata.

The leaves act like tiny factories. Sunlight provides the energy, and the plant combines water and carbon dioxide inside its leaves to produce a sugar called glucose, which the plant uses for energy and growth.
As a byproduct of this process, the plant releases oxygen into the air through the same stomata pores — the same oxygen that humans and animals breathe in every day.

title: Chapter 3: Chlorophyll — The Green Pigment
paragraphs: If you look closely at a leaf, you'll notice it's green. That color comes from a pigment called chlorophyll, which lives inside tiny structures in the leaf cells called chloroplasts.
Chlorophyll's job is to absorb sunlight. It's especially good at absorbing red and blue light, but it reflects green light back to our eyes — which is exactly why leaves look green to us.

Q: What is the primary pigment involved in photosynthesis? The answer is chlorophyll-a, found inside the chloroplasts of plant cells — it's the main pigment responsible for capturing light energy to power the entire process.
